topic_and_scope: This document reviews marine lipid biology and lipidomics, emphasizing the structural diversity of environmental lipids, their roles in marine food webs, and how climate change may alter lipid production, transfer, and bioactive properties, with discussion of biotechnological and biomarker approaches.
main_themes: Structural diversity and analytical approaches in marine lipids (lipid classes, lipidomics, and biomarkers).
Role of long-chain omega-3 PUFAs (EPA and DHA) and sterols in marine nutrition, physiology, and trophic transfer.
Climate change impacts on lipid production, distribution, trophic dynamics, and opportunities for algal biotechnology.
main_findings: Lipidomics enables comprehensive profiling of thousands of lipid molecular species in marine systems, supporting precise tracing of energy flow and trophic connections beyond bulk lipid measures.

Phytoplankton are the primary sources of long-chain omega-3 PUFAs (EPA and DHA) crucial for marine consumers and human nutrition; their production and transfer are sensitive to temperature, pH, and other climate-related factors, with potential cascading effects on food webs.

key_gaps.description: Explicit need to measure fatty acid unsaturation and absolute lipid concentrations on daily to seasonal time scales and to report lipids per unit biomass (mg g−1) to distinguish dietary from environmental responses.

Implied lack of detailed understanding of non-phytoplankton sources of ω3 LC-PUFAs (e.g., bacteria, thraustochytrids, some invertebrates) and their contribution to marine EFA subsidies and trophic modeling.

future_directions.title: Daily-to-seasonal lipidomics monitoring across key marine ecosystems
future_directions.rationale: The article emphasizes that lipid supply and composition respond to rapid climatic shifts (temperature, pH) and seasonal cycles. Implement high-frequency MS-based lipidomics with LC separation to quantify intact lipid molecular species, reported per weight (mg g−1) and as unsaturation indices, across multiple basins. Combine with concurrent environmental measurements (temperature, pH, nutrients) and trophic data to link PUFA availability to bloom events, vertical mixing, and energy transfer through the food web. This will provide robust baselines and detect early signs of disruption in PUFA provisioning to higher trophic levels and humans.

future_directions.title: Map de novo ω3 PUFA biosynthesis across invertebrate phyla
future_directions.rationale: The document notes that some invertebrates can synthesize ω3 PUFAs de novo, but the taxa and conditions remain unclear. Systematic genomics, transcriptomics, and functional assays should identify which species possess ωx desaturases or PKS-based pathways, under what environmental conditions they are expressed, and how these capacities scale with temperature and acidification. This work will refine ecological models of EFA supply and inform whether invertebrates can compensate for phytoplankton PUFA declines.

future_directions.title: Quantify PKS-derived PUFA flux from bacteria and thraustochytrids
future_directions.rationale: PKS pathways in thraustochytrids and cold-water bacteria can synthesize PUFAs without aerobic desaturation/elongation, potentially supplying EFAs under climate stress. Develop isotope-labeling and compound-specific isotope analyses to trace PKS-derived PUFAs through marine food webs, coupled with metagenomics/metatranscriptomics to map producer communities. Quantifying this subsidy will clarify alternative EFA sources when phytoplankton PUFA production declines.

future_directions.title: Standardize multi-tracer diet reconstruction in marine predators
future_directions.rationale: The review highlights the value of QFASA and sterol markers for dietary inferences but notes methodological refinement is needed. Extend QFASA by incorporating neutral vs polar lipid fractions and sterol profiles, validated through controlled feeding trials across representative species. Develop cross-species standardized protocols and databases to improve accuracy of predator–prey reconstructions in diverse ecosystems and under changing ocean conditions.

future_directions.title: Integrative lipidomics-genomics models under climate scenarios
future_directions.rationale: A key future direction is to couple lipidomic profiles across trophic levels with genomic and metagenomic data to predict how warming, stratification, and acidification alter lipid production, transfer, and fate. Build predictive models that incorporate gene pathways for PUFA biosynthesis, membrane remodeling, and lipid transport, linked to environmental drivers. Such models would forecast impacts on carbon transfer to deep waters and the availability of seafood ω3 LC-PUFAs for human consumption.

future_directions.title: Develop sustainable algal platforms for DHA/EPA production for aquaculture
future_directions.rationale: The document describes microalgae and thraustochytrids as rich sources of DHA/EPA and notes biotechnological applications. Advance scalable, low-cost production systems (including engineered microalgae and thraustochytrids) and integrate them into aquafeeds, with life-cycle analyses comparing with fish-oil inputs. Explore wastewater and carbon-capture synergies to enhance sustainability while maintaining or improving growth and PUFA yields.

future_directions.title: Investigate buoyancy, phase transitions, and carbon pumps under future ocean conditions
future_directions.rationale: Lipids such as wax esters and triacylglycerols drive buoyancy and phase transitions that affect vertical transport and carbon sequestration. Study how temperature and OA alter unsaturation, phase behavior, and buoyancy in key species (copepods, deep-sea zooplankton, and cetaceans) to understand implications for the lipid pump and deep-ocean carbon flux. Results will inform models of energy flow and climate feedbacks in marine systems.
